meta.title: Checking the study's same-software identifiers before the scanner queries them
meta.follows: ../results.json. Its data/classification.json judged 9 identifiers to be the same software as products in the scanner's table. This checks each against the CVEs it adds and against live NVD, before any was added.
meta.scanner_table_checked: src/phantomprobe/cpe_tables.py at commit 5904796 (the 0.9.3 table): 74 products, 19 with second identifiers, 25 second identifiers. The scripts read the table from src/, so running them against a later commit compares against the identifiers added as a result of this check.
method: scripts/1_extra_cves.py lists, from the study's NVD snapshot (../raw-feeds/), the CVEs each identifier holds that the table's identifiers lack, with the versions NVD files them under.
scripts/2_describe.py reads the NVD description of each of those CVEs, to judge whether it is a flaw in the product itself or in something filed against it.

scripts/3_live_check.py asks the live NVD CVE API what the scanner would ask: the unpadded CPE at one version, first under the table's identifiers and then under each new one, and counts what each new one returns beyond them.
The four identifiers no rule of the study proposed were found by rechecking, against the snapshot, the identifiers the 2026-11-16 pilot had measured at one version and left out as adding nothing.
scripts/4_version_gap.py explains, from the snapshot, why oracle:jre added more CVEs at Java 1.7.0 than it adds across all versions.
caveats: Whether a CVE is a flaw in the product was judged from its NVD description by one rater, the AI assistant that ran the check.
Snapshot counts are version-independent. Live counts are for one version and depend on NVD on the day.

The first live run met one HTTP 502 from NVD during the Java 1.6.0 queries. A rerun of Java 1.6.0 (data/live_recheck.json) returned the same counts for all four identifiers. The scanner does not retry a 502.
Only the identifiers named here were rechecked. Of the rest the pilot left out, nginx:nginx and varnish-cache:varnish hold nothing the table's identifiers lack at any version.

not_flaws_in_the_product.CVE-2021-21349: XStream, a third-party Java library, filed under java_se 7u321 and 8u311
not_flaws_in_the_product.CVE-2021-41041: Eclipse OpenJ9, another JVM, filed under java_se 8 and 11

per_identifier.decision: added: its two Java SE flaws are reached at 11.0.14; the two that are not Java SE flaws sit under version strings (7u321, 8u311, 8, 11) that the scanner never sends, since it reads dotted versions only

not_flaws_in_the_product.CVE-2014-6394: the send npm package, its 0.8.3 and earlier filed as Node.js versions
not_flaws_in_the_product.CVE-2014-7192: the syntax-error npm package, filed against Node.js 0.10.32 and earlier

per_identifier.decision: left out: neither CVE it adds is a Node.js flaw, and Node.js 0.8.3 would be reported with a 7.5 and a 10.0

not_flaws_in_the_product.CVE-2007-2407: Apple's Samba on Mac OS X 10.3.9 and 10.4.10, filed against every version

per_identifier.decision: left out: its one CVE is Apple's build, and it returned nothing for Samba 3.0.25 or 4.20.0

a_lookup_at_one_version_can_miss_more_th.example: oracle:jre holds 24 CVEs that oracle:jdk lacks at any version, yet asked about Java 1.7.0 it returned 52 that oracle:jdk:1.7.0 did not.
a_lookup_at_one_version_can_miss_more_th.why: Of those 52, 21 are not filed under oracle:jdk at all. The other 31 are, but only for older releases: their oracle:jre entries name 1.7.0 and their oracle:jdk entries do not. A version-independent count sees them as covered.
